movement.pick: Which art movement is {label} known for?
movement.match: Match each painter to the art movement they're known for.
movement.odd: Three of these painters are known for {value}. Which one isn't?
movement.reverse: Which of these painters is known for {value}?

rows.label: Andy Warhol
rows.description: American artist, film director, and producer (1928–1987)
rows.hook: turned soup cans and celebrity photos into famous silkscreen prints

rows.label: Salvador Dalí
rows.hook: painted melting clocks draped over a dreamlike landscape

rows.label: Banksy
rows.description: English graffiti artist, political activist, and painter
rows.hook: sprays anonymous stencils on city walls and once shredded his own painting at auction

rows.label: Claude Monet
rows.hook: painted glowing water lilies and haystacks in his garden

rows.label: Rembrandt
rows.hook: used dramatic light and shadow in portraits and a famous night-time militia scene

rows.label: Georgia O'Keeffe
rows.hook: painted oversized flowers and desert bones inspired by the New Mexico landscape

rows.label: Mark Rothko
rows.hook: filled huge canvases with glowing blocks of color meant to overwhelm the viewer

rows.label: Henri de Toulouse-Lautrec
rows.hook: captured cabaret dancers and nightlife in bold poster designs

rows.label: Pierre-Auguste Renoir
rows.hook: painted sunlit garden parties and dancers in warm, joyful colors

rows.label: Albrecht Dürer
rows.description: German painter, printmaker, mathematician, and theorist (1471-1528)
rows.hook: made incredibly detailed engravings, including a famous study of a rabbit

rows.label: M. C. Escher
rows.hook: drew impossible staircases and tessellated patterns that trick the eye

rows.label: René Magritte
rows.hook: painted men in bowler hats and a pipe labeled as not actually being a pipe

rows.label: Paul Cézanne
rows.hook: painted apples and mountains built from blocky geometric brushstrokes

rows.label: Egon Schiele
rows.hook: drew raw, angular nudes and intense self-portraits full of tension

rows.label: James McNeill Whistler
rows.hook: painted a famous portrait of his own mother and moody nighttime cityscapes

rows.label: Artemisia Gentileschi
rows.hook: painted dramatic biblical scenes with fierce, powerful women at their center

rows.label: Jacques-Louis David
rows.hook: painted heroic scenes of a famous emperor and dramatic moments from a revolution

rows.label: Edgar Degas
rows.hook: painted ballet dancers rehearsing and performing on stage

rows.label: Amedeo Modigliani
rows.hook: painted portraits with long, elegant necks and almond-shaped eyes

rows.label: Édouard Manet
rows.hook: shocked the art world with a bold nude figure in an outdoor picnic scene

rows.label: Joan Miró
rows.hook: filled his canvases with playful abstract shapes in bright primary colors

rows.label: Diego Velázquez
rows.hook: painted intimate scenes of a royal court, including a young princess and her attendants

rows.label: Mary Cassatt
rows.hook: painted tender scenes of mothers and children in quiet domestic moments

rows.label: Caspar David Friedrich
rows.hook: painted lone figures gazing out over vast, misty landscapes

rows.label: Eugène Delacroix
rows.hook: painted a bare-chested woman leading a crowd over barricades during an uprising

rows.label: Gustave Courbet
rows.hook: painted ordinary laborers and rural life exactly as he saw it, rejecting idealized styles

rows.label: Ilya Repin
rows.hook: painted exhausted laborers hauling a barge along a great river

rows.label: John James Audubon
rows.hook: created detailed, lifelike illustrations of birds found across a continent

rows.label: Giuseppe Arcimboldo
rows.description: Italian painter of the late Renaissance (1527–1593)
rows.hook: made portraits out of fruits, vegetables, and everyday objects arranged into faces

rows.label: Ivan Aivazovsky
rows.hook: painted dramatic stormy seas and ships tossed by powerful waves
